question:
A 86-year-old male with a smoking history of 10 pack-years presents with progressive dyspnea and a
dry cough that began approximately 8 months ago, coinciding with flooding in his apartment. He now
experiences shortness of breath after walking two blocks or climbing one flight of stairs, whereas he
previously had no such limitations. He has no pets at home. Physical examination reveals bilateral
crackles on auscultation, with no other significant findings. Chest CT demonstrates diffuse centrilobular
nodules with air trapping. Pulmonary function tests show an FEV1/FVC ratio of 60%. What is the most
appropriate next step in evaluation? Answer Choices: (A) Testing for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (B)
Pulmonary rehabilitation program enrollment (C) High-resolution CT with prone positioning (D) Serum
IgE testing for allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (E) Methacholine challenge test for airway
hyperresponsiveness (F) Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy (G) Air sampling for environmental
mold (H) Skin testing for environmental allergens (I) Trial of living away from the residence (J) Referral
for lung biopsy to evaluate for interstitial lung disease
 A. High-resolution CT with prone positioning
B. Trial of living away from the residence
C. Air sampling for environmental mold
D. Serum IgE testing for allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis
E. Pulmonary rehabilitation program enrollment
F. Testing for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency
G. Methacholine challenge test for airway hyperresponsiveness
H. Skin testing for environmental allergens

I. Referral for lung biopsy to evaluate for interstitial lung disease
J. Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsy
